newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SCA SEES POSSIBLE FINE PRICE HIKE SEPT-OCT.
newsitem.headline: SCA SEES POSSIBLE FINE PRICE HIKE SEPT-OCT.

text.p: Swedish forestry group SCA said on Thursday it could raise fine paper prices in September or October this year.
"It could be on the cards to raise prices on fine paper sometime in September or October," SCA chief executive Sverker Martin-Lof told Reuters in connection with an analyst meeting.
"But it also depends on how the stabilisation of raw materials prices goes."
Martin-Lof expected the stabilisation of pulp prices to be much calmer this time than at the latest price upturn in 1995.
"There is need for a certain price recovery but it could be a significantly calmer price development than many think. The July NorScan figure was not so convincing," he said.
The North American and Scandinavian (NorScan) pulp stocks, excluding Norway, rose by 126,000 tonnes in July to more than 1.65 million tonnes, sources said.
"At the time of the latest price upturn there was a lack of raw materials. That will probably not be the case this time," Martin-Lof said.

SCA posted a 35 percent rise in profit after financial items to 2.25 billion crowns a day earlier, including a capital gain of 425 million crowns, beating market expectations for a profit of 2.01 billion.
